english.title: British person broadcast from ship / aircraft / marine structure
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a British person,

(A)_[operate]_
(B)_[participate in the operation of]_

apparatus by means of which a broadcast was made

(C)_[from a ship, which is not British-registered, while it is on the high seas]_
(D)_[from an aircraft, which is not British-registered, while it is on or over the high seas]_
(E)_[from a structure, other than a ship, that was affixed to, or supported by, the bed of the high seas]_
(F)_[from an object on the high seas]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 80(1) and 93(1) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 80(2) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 provides that the offence does not apply to broadcasts made from a ship in contravention of section 79(1) of the Act; and to broadcasts made from a marine structure or other object in waters in a designated area.
(ii) Section 93(3) of the Act provides that proceedings in England and Wales for this offence may be brought only by OFCOM or by or with the consent of the Secretary of State or the DPP.
(iii) Section 110 of the Act provides for criminal liability of company directors, managers, etc.
(iv) Section 94 of the Act provides a saving for broadcasts made under and in accordance with a wireless telegraphy licence.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022, see paragraph 16 of Schedule 8 to the Act; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 35(2)(a) of the Act and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
